newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Jan M2 money supply up 18.1 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Jan M2 money supply up 18.1 pct yr/yr.

text.p: South Korea's M2 money supply rose 18.1 percent in January year-on-year, against 12.5 percent growth a year earlier, the Bank of Korea said on Thursday.

NOTE: M2 consists of money in circulation, checking account and savings account deposits with banks. The bank uses MCT -- an aggregate of M2, certificates of deposit and money in trust accounts -- as one of the main indicators for money supply.
The central bank said January M2 growth was higher than a year ago because a large amount of deposits shifted from trust accounts to savings accounts in banks.
It said money in trust accounts had fallen since last May when their maturity was extended by up to six months.
MCT grew 18.5 percent in January, against a 21.5 percent rise a year ago, it said.
Time deposits with banks fell by 972.7 billion won in January while CDs and money in trust accounts rose by a combined 2.52 trillion won, it said.
Interest rates fell by the end of January despite the financial failure of Hanbo Steel Co, which was declared insolvent on January 23 due to heavy debts.

Yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds ended the month at 12 percent, compared with 12.60 percent at the end of December. The overnight call rate fell to an average of 11.67 percent at end-January from 12.20 percent.
